name: HM Courts & Tribunals Service Civil Money Claims (moneyclaims.service.gov.uk)

arguments.query: site.gov.uk moneyclaims.service.gov.uk civil money claims contact refund court fees complaints HMCTS
arguments.objective: Find official Civil Money Claims contact email and hours, court fee refund rules and deadlines, HMCTS complaints stages response times and ombudsman.
Find ordinary Civil Money Claims fee refund or nonrefund rules, cancellation, Help with Fees retrospective deadline and official service terms.
Find Money Claims terms and conditions refund clauses and service identity; prioritise official terms page.

dossier.summary: HM Courts & Tribunals Service Civil Money Claims provides an online money-claim service with email and telephone support. Court-fee refunds include retrospective Help with Fees applications within three months and a separate scheme for specified overcharged or mischarged fees. Service complaints progress through an initial response, senior-manager review and User Investigations Team appeal, with subsequent referral through an MP to the Parliamentary and Health Service Ombudsman.

facts.statement: The Money Claims website describes its online service as being developed and improved through user feedback.
facts.quote: We are building a new service. Different designs are being tested and changed based on feedback from users.

facts.statement: Money Claims accepts support enquiries by email at contactocmc@justice.gov.uk and by telephone on 0300 123 7050, Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 5pm.
facts.quote:
Contact us for help
Email
contactocmc@justice.gov.uk
Telephone
0300 123 7050
Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 5pm.

facts.statement: Retrospective Help with Fees requires both payment within the last three months and eligibility for help when the fee was paid.
facts.quote:
If you’ve already paid the fee, you can apply to get money back if both of the following apply:
you paid the fee in the last 3 months
you were eligible for help when you paid it

facts.statement: An application for help with an already-paid fee must be sent to the court or tribunal that received the fee.
facts.quote: If you’re applying for money off a fee you’ve already paid, send your help with fees application to the court or tribunal you paid your fee to.

facts.statement: The separate Ministry of Justice court-fee refund scheme addresses overcharged and mischarged fees.
facts.quote:
overcharged – where we have charged a fee that is greater than the cost of the service
mischarged – where we have charged the wrong fee or we should not have charged a fee at all

facts.statement: Eligibility for that refund scheme is limited to circumstances and fees specified in its guidance, rather than every court-fee payment.
facts.quote: You can only claim a refund if your circumstances and the fee you paid are referred to in the guidance document.

facts.statement: The scheme covers applicants who paid the court directly or were ordered to pay the fees of someone who brought a claim against them.
facts.quote:
You can only claim a refund if:
you paid the fee straight to the court
someone put a claim against you and you were ordered to pay their fees

facts.statement: Applications under the specified-fee refund scheme must use one of its designated refund forms.
facts.quote:
You must apply for a refund using either:
application for full or partial refund of court fees
low value personal injury (LVPI) Part 8 stage 3 refund form
All applications must be submitted using these forms.

facts.statement: Refund-scheme applications and evidence are accepted by email at civil_refunds@justice.gov.uk.
facts.quote:
Send the form and your evidence as email attachments to
civil_refunds@justice.gov.uk

facts.statement: Refund application emails should have the subject “Civil fees refund application”, with attachments within a 10MB email limit.
facts.quote:
The email size limit is 10MB but you can send more than one email.
Write ‘Civil fees refund application’ as the subject.

facts.statement: Refund-scheme applications can alternatively be posted to HMCTS, PO Box 8793, Leicester, LE1 8BN.
facts.quote:
Post the form and your evidence to:
HMCTS
PO Box 8793
Leicester
LE1 8BN

facts.statement: The refund scheme aims to process applications within 20 working days of receipt.
facts.quote: We will try to process your application in 20 working days from the day we get it.

facts.statement: The refund-scheme contact team aims to respond to enquiries within five working days.
facts.quote:
Email
civil_refunds@justice.gov.uk
We aim to respond within 5 working days.

facts.statement: Refund applicants receive an email or letter explaining missing information, the decision, payment details or rejection reasons.
facts.quote:
You’ll be told by email or letter:
if any information is missing
whether your claim is successful
the refund amount and when it’ll be paid
the reasons for any rejection

facts.statement: HMCTS service complaints concern staff handling and cannot change a case decision or investigate judicial conduct.
facts.quote: Our complaint process looks at how your case was handled by our staff. We’re not able to change the decision in your case or investigate how a judge or magistrate acted towards you.

facts.statement: HMCTS accepts complaints through an online form, in person, by email, by phone or in writing.
facts.quote:
To complain about our service:
complete our online complaints form
speak to a member of staff in our buildings and we’ll record your feedback
contact our courts or tribunals by email, phone or in writing

facts.statement: The initial complaint response target is 10 working days.
facts.quote: We aim to respond within 10 working days.

facts.statement: A dissatisfied complainant can request a senior-manager review, explain their dissatisfaction and expect a target response within 10 working days.
facts.quote: you can ask a senior manager at the office to carry out a review. You should explain why you’re not satisfied. The manager will aim to respond to you within 10 working days.

facts.statement: After senior-manager review, a complainant can appeal to the User Investigations Team, whose contact details are supplied by the reviewing manager.
facts.quote: If you’re not satisfied with the senior manager’s review of your complaint, you can appeal to the User Investigations Team. The manager who reviewed your complaint will give you their contact details.

facts.statement: The User Investigations Team reviews the handling of the complaint and aims to respond within 15 working days.
facts.quote: The User Investigations Team will take a fresh look at the way your complaint has been handled. They will aim to respond to you within 15 working days.

facts.statement: After completing the HMCTS complaints process, a complainant can ask their MP to refer the case to the Parliamentary and Health Service Ombudsman.
facts.quote:
If you remain unsatisfied at the end of the HMCTS complaints process, you can also ask your member of Parliament to refer your case to the
Parliamentary and Health Service Ombudsman

facts.statement: HMCTS uses plain, direct language that acknowledges dissatisfaction and explains practical next steps.
facts.quote: If you’re not happy with the reply to your complaint, you can ask a senior manager at the office to carry out a review. You should explain why you’re not satisfied.

persona.voice: Write in plain, neutral public-service English, addressing the customer as “you” and the service as “we”. Acknowledge dissatisfaction and give clear, practical next steps in short paragraphs or lists. Distinguish staff-service complaints from judicial decisions, and describe published response times as aims rather than guarantees.
